a:r.a:t: Currently, we use Mimeo and Solo for service virtualization. Under the hood, they both use Mountebank - a Node.js-based mock server.
Mountebank is a great tool. It has a well-designed API, a flexible configuration format, and supports advanced features like JSONPath predicates, proxy modes, and JavaScript behaviors.

The configuration format you see here is probably familiar to many of you. You define imposters that listen on ports, stubs that match requests, predicates that filter requests, and responses that define what to return.

This format is powerful and expressive. The problem isn't the API design - it's the implementation performance. Mountebank runs on Node.js, which means JavaScript interpretation overhead, single-threaded event loop limitations, garbage collection pauses, and slow JSON/XML processing.
What if we could keep this exact configuration format but make it 20 to 250 times faster?
